attribute.name: seller
attribute.description: An entity which offers (sells / leases / lends / loans) the services / goods. A seller may also be a provider.

attribute.name: sender
attribute.description: A sub property of participant. The participant who is at the sending end of the action.

attribute.name: sensoryRequirement
attribute.description: A description of any sensory requirements and levels necessary to function on the job, including hearing and vision. Defined terms such as those in O*net may be used, but note that there is no way to specify the level of ability as well as its nature when using a defined term.

attribute.name: sensoryUnit
attribute.description: The neurological pathway extension that inputs and sends information to the brain or spinal cord.

attribute.name: serialNumber
attribute.description: The serial number or any alphanumeric identifier of a particular product. When attached to an offer, it is a shortcut for the serial number of the product included in the offer.

attribute.name: seriousAdverseOutcome
attribute.description: A possible serious complication and/or serious side effect of this therapy. Serious adverse outcomes include those that are life-threatening; result in death, disability, or permanent damage; require hospitalization or prolong existing hospitalization; cause congenital anomalies or birth defects; or jeopardize the patient and may require medical or surgical intervention to prevent one of the outcomes in this definition.

attribute.name: serverStatus
attribute.description: Status of a game server.

attribute.name: servesCuisine
attribute.description: The cuisine of the restaurant.

attribute.name: serviceArea
attribute.description: The geographic area where the service is provided.

attribute.name: serviceAudience
attribute.description: The audience eligible for this service.

attribute.name: serviceLocation
attribute.description: The location (e.g. civic structure, local business, etc.) where a person can go to access the service.

attribute.name: serviceOperator
attribute.description: The operating organization, if different from the provider. This enables the representation of services that are provided by an organization, but operated by another organization like a subcontractor.

attribute.name: serviceOutput
attribute.description: The tangible thing generated by the service, e.g. a passport, permit, etc.

attribute.name: servicePhone
attribute.description: The phone number to use to access the service.

attribute.name: servicePostalAddress
attribute.description: The address for accessing the service by mail.

attribute.name: serviceSmsNumber
attribute.description: The number to access the service by text message.

attribute.name: serviceType
attribute.description: The type of service being offered, e.g. veterans' benefits, emergency relief, etc.

attribute.name: serviceUrl
attribute.description: The website to access the service.

attribute.name: servingSize
attribute.description: The serving size, in terms of the number of volume or mass.

attribute.name: sha256
attribute.description: The [SHA-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SHA-2) SHA256 hash of the content of the item. For example, a zero-length input has value 'e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855'.

attribute.name: sharedContent
attribute.description: A CreativeWork such as an image, video, or audio clip shared as part of this posting.

attribute.name: shippingConditions
attribute.description: The conditions (constraints, price) applicable to the [[ShippingService]].

attribute.name: shippingDestination
attribute.description: indicates (possibly multiple) shipping destinations. These can be defined in several ways, e.g. postalCode ranges.

attribute.name: shippingDetails
attribute.description: Indicates information about the shipping policies and options associated with an [[Offer]].

attribute.name: shippingOrigin
attribute.description: Indicates the origin of a shipment, i.e. where it should be coming from.

attribute.name: shippingRate
attribute.description: The shipping rate is the cost of shipping to the specified destination. Typically, the maxValue and currency values (of the [[MonetaryAmount]]) are most appropriate.

attribute.name: sibling
attribute.description: A sibling of the person.

attribute.name: siblings
attribute.description: A sibling of the person.

attribute.name: signDetected
attribute.description: A sign detected by the test.

attribute.name: signOrSymptom
attribute.description: A sign or symptom of this condition. Signs are objective or physically observable manifestations of the medical condition while symptoms are the subjective experience of the medical condition.

attribute.name: significance
attribute.description: The significance associated with the superficial anatomy; as an example, how characteristics of the superficial anatomy can suggest underlying medical conditions or courses of treatment.

attribute.name: significantLink
attribute.description: One of the more significant URLs on the page. Typically, these are the non-navigation links that are clicked on the most.

attribute.name: significantLinks
attribute.description: The most significant URLs on the page. Typically, these are the non-navigation links that are clicked on the most.

attribute.name: size
attribute.description: A standardized size of a product or creative work, specified either through a simple textual string (for example 'XL', '32Wx34L'), a QuantitativeValue with a unitCode, or a comprehensive and structured [[SizeSpecification]]; in other cases, the [[width]], [[height]], [[depth]] and [[weight]] properties may be more applicable.

attribute.name: sizeGroup
attribute.description: The size group (also known as "size type") for a product's size. Size groups are common in the fashion industry to define size segments and suggested audiences for wearable products. Multiple values can be combined, for example "men's big and tall", "petite maternity" or "regular".

attribute.name: sizeSystem
attribute.description: The size system used to identify a product's size. Typically either a standard (for example, "GS1" or "ISO-EN13402"), country code (for example "US" or "JP"), or a measuring system (for example "Metric" or "Imperial").

attribute.name: skills
attribute.description: A statement of knowledge, skill, ability, task or any other assertion expressing a competency that is either claimed by a person, an organization or desired or required to fulfill a role or to work in an occupation.

attribute.name: sku
attribute.description: The Stock Keeping Unit (SKU), i.e. a merchant-specific identifier for a product or service, or the product to which the offer refers.

attribute.name: slogan
attribute.description: A slogan or motto associated with the item.

attribute.name: smiles
attribute.description: A specification in form of a line notation for describing the structure of chemical species using short ASCII strings. Double bond stereochemistry \ indicators may need to be escaped in the string in formats where the backslash is an escape character.

attribute.name: smokingAllowed
attribute.description: Indicates whether it is allowed to smoke in the place, e.g. in the restaurant, hotel or hotel room.

attribute.name: sodiumContent
attribute.description: The number of milligrams of sodium.

attribute.name: softwareAddOn
attribute.description: Additional content for a software application.

attribute.name: softwareHelp
attribute.description: Software application help.

attribute.name: softwareRequirements
attribute.description: Component dependency requirements for application. This includes runtime environments and shared libraries that are not included in the application distribution package, but required to run the application (examples: DirectX, Java or .NET runtime).

attribute.name: softwareVersion
attribute.description: Version of the software instance.

attribute.name: source
attribute.description: The source or cause of the event.

attribute.name: sourceOrganization
attribute.description: The Organization on whose behalf the creator was working.

attribute.name: sourcedFrom
attribute.description: The neurological pathway that originates the neurons.

attribute.name: spatial
attribute.description: The "spatial" property can be used in cases when more specific properties (e.g. [[locationCreated]], [[spatialCoverage]], [[contentLocation]]) are not known to be appropriate.

attribute.name: spatialCoverage
attribute.description: The spatialCoverage of a CreativeWork indicates the place(s) which are the focus of the content. It is a subproperty of contentLocation intended primarily for more technical and detailed materials. For example with a Dataset, it indicates areas that the dataset describes: a dataset of New York weather would have spatialCoverage which was the place: the state of New York.

attribute.name: speakable
attribute.description:
Indicates sections of a Web page that are particularly 'speakable' in the sense of being highlighted as being especially appropriate for text-to-speech conversion. Other sections of a page may also be usefully spoken in particular circumstances; the 'speakable' property serves to indicate the parts most likely to be generally useful for speech.
The *speakable* property can be repeated an arbitrary number of times, with three kinds of possible 'content-locator' values:
1.) *id-value* URL references - uses *id-value* of an element in the page being annotated. The simplest use of *speakable* has (potentially relative) URL values, referencing identified sections of the document concerned.
2.) CSS Selectors - addresses content in the annotated page, e.g. via class attribute. Use the [[cssSelector]] property.
3.) XPaths - addresses content via XPaths (assuming an XML view of the content). Use the [[xpath]] property.
For more sophisticated markup of speakable sections beyond simple ID references, either CSS selectors or XPath expressions to pick out document section(s) as speakable. For this we define a supporting type, [[SpeakableSpecification]] which is defined to be a possible value of the *speakable* property.

attribute.name: specialCommitments
attribute.description: Any special commitments associated with this job posting. Valid entries include VeteranCommit, MilitarySpouseCommit, etc.

attribute.name: specialOpeningHoursSpecification
attribute.description: The special opening hours of a certain place.\n\nUse this to explicitly override general opening hours brought in scope by [[openingHoursSpecification]] or [[openingHours]].

attribute.name: specialty
attribute.description: One of the domain specialities to which this web page's content applies.

attribute.name: speechToTextMarkup
attribute.description: Form of markup used. eg. [SSML](https://www.w3.org/TR/speech-synthesis11) or [IPA](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Property:P898).

attribute.name: speed
attribute.description:
The speed range of the vehicle. If the vehicle is powered by an engine, the upper limit of the speed range (indicated by [[maxValue]]) should be the maximum speed achievable under regular conditions.

Typical unit code(s): KMH for km/h, HM for mile per hour (0.447 04 m/s), KNT for knot

*Note 1: Use [[minValue]] and [[maxValue]] to indicate the range. Typically, the minimal value is zero.
* Note 2: There are many different ways of measuring the speed range. You can link to information about how the given value has been determined using the [[valueReference]] property.

attribute.name: spokenByCharacter
attribute.description: The (e.g. fictional) character, Person or Organization to whom the quotation is attributed within the containing CreativeWork.

attribute.name: sponsor
attribute.description: A person or organization that supports a thing through a pledge, promise, or financial contribution. E.g. a sponsor of a Medical Study or a corporate sponsor of an event.
attribute.applies_to: MedicalStudy, Event, Organization, Person, CreativeWork, Grant

attribute.name: sport
attribute.description: A type of sport (e.g. Baseball).

attribute.name: sportsActivityLocation
attribute.description: A sub property of location. The sports activity location where this action occurred.

attribute.name: sportsEvent
attribute.description: A sub property of location. The sports event where this action occurred.

attribute.name: sportsTeam
attribute.description: A sub property of participant. The sports team that participated on this action.

attribute.name: spouse
attribute.description: The person's spouse.

attribute.name: stage
attribute.description: The stage of the condition, if applicable.

attribute.name: stageAsNumber
attribute.description: The stage represented as a number, e.g. 3.

attribute.name: starRating
attribute.description: An official rating for a lodging business or food establishment, e.g. from national associations or standards bodies. Use the author property to indicate the rating organization, e.g. as an Organization with name such as (e.g. HOTREC, DEHOGA, WHR, or Hotelstars).

attribute.name: startDate
attribute.description: The start date and time of the item (in [ISO 8601 date format](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601)).
attribute.applies_to: Role, DatedMoneySpecification, Event, CreativeWorkSeries, EducationalOccupationalProgram, MerchantReturnPolicySeasonalOverride, Schedule, CreativeWorkSeason

attribute.name: startOffset
attribute.description: The start time of the clip expressed as the number of seconds from the beginning of the work.

attribute.name: startTime
attribute.description: The startTime of something. For a reserved event or service (e.g. FoodEstablishmentReservation), the time that it is expected to start. For actions that span a period of time, when the action was performed. E.g. John wrote a book from *January* to December. For media, including audio and video, it's the time offset of the start of a clip within a larger file.\n\nNote that Event uses startDate/endDate instead of startTime/endTime, even when describing dates with times. This situation may be clarified in future revisions.

attribute.name: statType
attribute.description: Indicates the kind of statistic represented by a [[StatisticalVariable]], e.g. mean, count etc. The value of statType is a property, either from within Schema.org (e.g. [[median]], [[marginOfError]], [[maxValue]], [[minValue]]) or from other compatible (e.g. RDF) systems such as DataCommons.org or Wikidata.org.

attribute.name: status
attribute.description: The status of the study (enumerated).

attribute.name: steeringPosition
attribute.description: The position of the steering wheel or similar device (mostly for cars).

attribute.name: step
attribute.description: A single step item (as HowToStep, text, document, video, etc.) or a HowToSection.

attribute.name: stepValue
attribute.description: The stepValue attribute indicates the granularity that is expected (and required) of the value in a PropertyValueSpecification.

attribute.name: steps
attribute.description: A single step item (as HowToStep, text, document, video, etc.) or a HowToSection (originally misnamed 'steps'; 'step' is preferred).

attribute.name: storageRequirements
attribute.description: Storage requirements (free space required).

attribute.name: streetAddress
attribute.description: The street address. For example, 1600 Amphitheatre Pkwy.

attribute.name: strengthUnit
attribute.description: The units of an active ingredient's strength, e.g. mg.

attribute.name: strengthValue
attribute.description: The value of an active ingredient's strength, e.g. 325.

attribute.name: structuralClass
attribute.description: The name given to how bone physically connects to each other.

attribute.name: study
attribute.description: A medical study or trial related to this entity.

attribute.name: studyDesign
attribute.description: Specifics about the observational study design (enumerated).

attribute.name: studyLocation
attribute.description: The location in which the study is taking/took place.

attribute.name: studySubject
attribute.description: A subject of the study, i.e. one of the medical conditions, therapies, devices, drugs, etc. investigated by the study.

attribute.name: subEvent
attribute.description: An Event that is part of this event. For example, a conference event includes many presentations, each of which is a subEvent of the conference.

attribute.name: subEvents
attribute.description: Events that are a part of this event. For example, a conference event includes many presentations, each subEvents of the conference.

attribute.name: subOrganization
attribute.description: A relationship between two organizations where the first includes the second, e.g., as a subsidiary. See also: the more specific 'department' property.

attribute.name: subReservation
attribute.description: The individual reservations included in the package. Typically a repeated property.

attribute.name: subStageSuffix
attribute.description: The substage, e.g. 'a' for Stage IIIa.

attribute.name: subStructure
attribute.description: Component (sub-)structure(s) that comprise this anatomical structure.

attribute.name: subTest
attribute.description: A component test of the panel.

attribute.name: subTrip
attribute.description: Identifies a [[Trip]] that is a subTrip of this Trip. For example Day 1, Day 2, etc. of a multi-day trip.

attribute.name: subjectOf
attribute.description: A CreativeWork or Event about this Thing.

attribute.name: subtitleLanguage
attribute.description: Languages in which subtitles/captions are available, in [IETF BCP 47 standard format](http://tools.ietf.org/html/bcp47).

attribute.name: successorOf
attribute.description: A pointer from a newer variant of a product to its previous, often discontinued predecessor.

attribute.name: sugarContent
attribute.description: The number of grams of sugar.

attribute.name: suggestedAge
attribute.description: The age or age range for the intended audience or person, for example 3-12 months for infants, 1-5 years for toddlers.

attribute.name: suggestedAnswer
attribute.description: An answer (possibly one of several, possibly incorrect) to a Question, e.g. on a Question/Answer site.

attribute.name: suggestedGender
attribute.description: The suggested gender of the intended person or audience, for example "male", "female", or "unisex".

attribute.name: suggestedMaxAge
attribute.description: Maximum recommended age in years for the audience or user.

attribute.name: suggestedMeasurement
attribute.description: A suggested range of body measurements for the intended audience or person, for example inseam between 32 and 34 inches or height between 170 and 190 cm. Typically found on a size chart for wearable products.

attribute.name: suggestedMinAge
attribute.description: Minimum recommended age in years for the audience or user.

attribute.name: suitableForDiet
attribute.description: Indicates a dietary restriction or guideline for which this recipe or menu item is suitable, e.g. diabetic, halal etc.

attribute.name: superEvent
attribute.description: An event that this event is a part of. For example, a collection of individual music performances might each have a music festival as their superEvent.

attribute.name: supersededBy
attribute.description: Relates a term (i.e. a property, class or enumeration) to one that supersedes it.

attribute.name: supply
attribute.description: A sub-property of instrument. A supply consumed when performing instructions or a direction.

attribute.name: supplyTo
attribute.description: The area to which the artery supplies blood.

attribute.name: supportingData
attribute.description: Supporting data for a SoftwareApplication.

attribute.name: surface
attribute.description: A material used as a surface in some artwork, e.g. Canvas, Paper, Wood, Board, etc.

attribute.name: syllabusSections
attribute.description: Indicates (typically several) Syllabus entities that lay out what each section of the overall course will cover.

attribute.name: target
attribute.description: Indicates a target EntryPoint, or url, for an Action.

attribute.name: targetCollection
attribute.description: A sub property of object. The collection target of the action.

attribute.name: targetDescription
attribute.description: The description of a node in an established educational framework.

attribute.name: targetName
attribute.description: The name of a node in an established educational framework.

attribute.name: targetPlatform
attribute.description: Type of app development: phone, Metro style, desktop, XBox, etc.

attribute.name: targetPopulation
attribute.description: Characteristics of the population for which this is intended, or which typically uses it, e.g. 'adults'.

attribute.name: targetProduct
attribute.description: Target Operating System / Product to which the code applies. If applies to several versions, just the product name can be used.

attribute.name: targetUrl
attribute.description: The URL of a node in an established educational framework.

attribute.name: taxID
attribute.description: The Tax / Fiscal ID of the organization or person, e.g. the TIN in the US or the CIF/NIF in Spain.

attribute.name: taxonRank
attribute.description: The taxonomic rank of this taxon given preferably as a URI from a controlled vocabulary – typically the ranks from TDWG TaxonRank ontology or equivalent Wikidata URIs.

attribute.name: taxonomicRange
attribute.description: The taxonomic grouping of the organism that expresses, encodes, or in some way related to the BioChemEntity.

attribute.name: teaches
attribute.description: The item being described is intended to help a person learn the competency or learning outcome defined by the referenced term.

attribute.name: telephone
attribute.description: The telephone number.

attribute.name: temporal
attribute.description: The "temporal" property can be used in cases where more specific properties (e.g. [[temporalCoverage]], [[dateCreated]], [[dateModified]], [[datePublished]]) are not known to be appropriate.

attribute.name: temporalCoverage
attribute.description:
The temporalCoverage of a CreativeWork indicates the period that the content applies to, i.e. that it describes, either as a DateTime or as a textual string indicating a time period in [ISO 8601 time interval format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601#Time_intervals). In the case of a Dataset it will typically indicate the relevant time period in a precise notation (e.g. for a 2011 census dataset, the year 2011 would be written "2011/2012"). Other forms of content, e.g. ScholarlyArticle, Book, TVSeries or TVEpisode, may indicate their temporalCoverage in broader terms - textually or via well-known URL. Written works such as books may sometimes have precise temporal coverage too, e.g. a work set in 1939 - 1945 can be indicated in ISO 8601 interval format format via "1939/1945".
Open-ended date ranges can be written with ".." in place of the end date. For example, "2015-11/.." indicates a range beginning in November 2015 and with no specified final date. This is tentative and might be updated in future when ISO 8601 is officially updated.

attribute.name: termCode
attribute.description: A code that identifies this [[DefinedTerm]] within a [[DefinedTermSet]].

attribute.name: termDuration
attribute.description: The amount of time in a term as defined by the institution. A term is a length of time where students take one or more classes. Semesters and quarters are common units for term.

attribute.name: termsOfService
attribute.description: Human-readable terms of service documentation.

attribute.name: termsPerYear
attribute.description: The number of times terms of study are offered per year. Semesters and quarters are common units for term. For example, if the student can only take 2 semesters for the program in one year, then termsPerYear should be 2.

attribute.name: text
attribute.description: The textual content of this CreativeWork.

attribute.name: textValue
attribute.description: Text value being annotated.

attribute.name: thumbnail
attribute.description: Thumbnail image for an image or video.

attribute.name: thumbnailUrl
attribute.description: A thumbnail image relevant to the Thing.

attribute.name: tickerSymbol
attribute.description: The exchange traded instrument associated with a Corporation object. The tickerSymbol is expressed as an exchange and an instrument name separated by a space character. For the exchange component of the tickerSymbol attribute, we recommend using the controlled vocabulary of Market Identifier Codes (MIC) specified in ISO 15022.

attribute.name: ticketNumber
attribute.description: The unique identifier for the ticket.

attribute.name: ticketToken
attribute.description: Reference to an asset (e.g., Barcode, QR code image or PDF) usable for entrance.

attribute.name: ticketedSeat
attribute.description: The seat associated with the ticket.

attribute.name: timeOfDay
attribute.description: The time of day the program normally runs. For example, "evenings".

attribute.name: timeRequired
attribute.description: Approximate or typical time it usually takes to work with or through the content of this work for the typical or target audience.

attribute.name: timeToComplete
attribute.description: The expected length of time to complete the program if attending full-time.

attribute.name: timestamp
attribute.description: The instant the event occured.

attribute.name: tissueSample
attribute.description: The type of tissue sample required for the test.

attribute.name: title
attribute.description: The title of the job.

attribute.name: titleEIDR
attribute.description:
An [EIDR](https://eidr.org/) (Entertainment Identifier Registry) [[identifier]] representing at the most general/abstract level, a work of film or television.
For example, the motion picture known as "Ghostbusters" has a titleEIDR of "10.5240/7EC7-228A-510A-053E-CBB8-J". This title (or work) may have several variants, which EIDR calls "edits". See [[editEIDR]].
Since schema.org types like [[Movie]], [[TVEpisode]], [[TVSeason]], and [[TVSeries]] can be used for both works and their multiple expressions, it is possible to use [[titleEIDR]] alone (for a general description), or alongside [[editEIDR]] for a more edit-specific description.

attribute.name: toLocation
attribute.description: A sub property of location. The final location of the object or the agent after the action.

attribute.name: toRecipient
attribute.description: A sub property of recipient. The recipient who was directly sent the message.

attribute.name: tocContinuation
attribute.description: A [[HyperTocEntry]] can have a [[tocContinuation]] indicated, which is another [[HyperTocEntry]] that would be the default next item to play or render.

attribute.name: tocEntry
attribute.description: Indicates a [[HyperTocEntry]] in a [[HyperToc]].

attribute.name: tongueWeight
attribute.description:
The permitted vertical load (TWR) of a trailer attached to the vehicle. Also referred to as Tongue Load Rating (TLR) or Vertical Load Rating (VLR).

Typical unit code(s): KGM for kilogram, LBR for pound

* Note 1: You can indicate additional information in the [[name]] of the [[QuantitativeValue]] node.
* Note 2: You may also link to a [[QualitativeValue]] node that provides additional information using [[valueReference]].
* Note 3: Note that you can use [[minValue]] and [[maxValue]] to indicate ranges.

attribute.name: tool
attribute.description: A sub property of instrument. An object used (but not consumed) when performing instructions or a direction.

attribute.name: torque
attribute.description:
The torque (turning force) of the vehicle's engine.

Typical unit code(s): NU for newton metre (N m), F17 for pound-force per foot, or F48 for pound-force per inch

* Note 1: You can link to information about how the given value has been determined (e.g. reference RPM) using the [[valueReference]] property.
* Note 2: You can use [[minValue]] and [[maxValue]] to indicate ranges.

attribute.name: totalHistoricalEnrollment
attribute.description: The total number of students that have enrolled in the history of the course.

attribute.name: totalJobOpenings
attribute.description: The number of positions open for this job posting. Use a positive integer. Do not use if the number of positions is unclear or not known.

attribute.name: totalPaymentDue
attribute.description: The total amount due.

attribute.name: totalPrice
attribute.description:
The total price for the reservation or ticket, including applicable taxes, shipping, etc.

Usage guidelines:

* Use values from 0123456789 (Unicode 'DIGIT ZERO' (U+0030) to 'DIGIT NINE' (U+0039)) rather than superficially similar Unicode symbols.
* Use '.' (Unicode 'FULL STOP' (U+002E)) rather than ',' to indicate a decimal point. Avoid using these symbols as a readability separator.

attribute.name: totalTime
attribute.description: The total time required to perform instructions or a direction (including time to prepare the supplies), in [ISO 8601 duration format](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601).

attribute.name: tourBookingPage
attribute.description: A page providing information on how to book a tour of some [[Place]], such as an [[Accommodation]] or [[ApartmentComplex]] in a real estate setting, as well as other kinds of tours as appropriate.

attribute.name: touristType
attribute.description: Attraction suitable for type(s) of tourist. E.g. children, visitors from a particular country, etc.

attribute.name: track
attribute.description: A music recording (track)—usually a single song. If an ItemList is given, the list should contain items of type MusicRecording.

attribute.name: trackingNumber
attribute.description: Shipper tracking number.

attribute.name: trackingUrl
attribute.description: Tracking url for the parcel delivery.

attribute.name: tracks
attribute.description: A music recording (track)—usually a single song.

attribute.name: trailer
attribute.description: The trailer of a movie or TV/radio series, season, episode, etc.
attribute.applies_to: TVSeries, Episode, Movie, CreativeWorkSeason, MovieSeries, VideoGameSeries, RadioSeries, VideoGame

attribute.name: trailerWeight
attribute.description:
The permitted weight of a trailer attached to the vehicle.

Typical unit code(s): KGM for kilogram, LBR for pound
* Note 1: You can indicate additional information in the [[name]] of the [[QuantitativeValue]] node.
* Note 2: You may also link to a [[QualitativeValue]] node that provides additional information using [[valueReference]].
* Note 3: Note that you can use [[minValue]] and [[maxValue]] to indicate ranges.

attribute.name: trainName
attribute.description: The name of the train (e.g. The Orient Express).

attribute.name: trainNumber
attribute.description: The unique identifier for the train.

attribute.name: trainingSalary
attribute.description: The estimated salary earned while in the program.

attribute.name: transFatContent
attribute.description: The number of grams of trans fat.

attribute.name: transcript
attribute.description: If this MediaObject is an AudioObject or VideoObject, the transcript of that object.

attribute.name: transitTime
attribute.description:
The typical delay the order has been sent for delivery and the goods reach the final customer.
In the context of [[ShippingDeliveryTime]], use the [[QuantitativeValue]]. Typical properties: minValue, maxValue, unitCode (d for DAY).
In the context of [[ShippingConditions]], use the [[ServicePeriod]]. It has a duration (as a [[QuantitativeValue]]) and also business days and a cut-off time.

attribute.name: translationOfWork
attribute.description: The work that this work has been translated from. E.g. 物种起源 is a translationOf “On the Origin of Species”.

attribute.name: translator
attribute.description: Organization or person who adapts a creative work to different languages, regional differences and technical requirements of a target market, or that translates during some event.

attribute.name: transmissionMethod
attribute.description: How the disease spreads, either as a route or vector, for example 'direct contact', 'Aedes aegypti', etc.

attribute.name: travelBans
attribute.description: Information about travel bans, e.g. in the context of a pandemic.

attribute.name: trialDesign
attribute.description: Specifics about the trial design (enumerated).

attribute.name: tributary
attribute.description: The anatomical or organ system that the vein flows into; a larger structure that the vein connects to.

attribute.name: tripOrigin
attribute.description: The location of origin of the trip, prior to any destination(s).

attribute.name: typeOfBed
attribute.description: The type of bed to which the BedDetail refers, i.e. the type of bed available in the quantity indicated by quantity.

attribute.name: typeOfGood
attribute.description: The product that this structured value is referring to.

attribute.name: typicalAgeRange
attribute.description: The typical expected age range, e.g. '7-9', '11-'.

attribute.name: typicalCreditsPerTerm
attribute.description: The number of credits or units a full-time student would be expected to take in 1 term however 'term' is defined by the institution.

attribute.name: typicalTest

attribute.name: usageInfo
attribute.description:
The schema.org [[usageInfo]] property indicates further information about a [[CreativeWork]]. This property is applicable both to works that are freely available and to those that require payment or other transactions. It can reference additional information, e.g. community expectations on preferred linking and citation conventions, as well as purchasing details. For something that can be commercially licensed, usageInfo can provide detailed, resource-specific information about licensing options.
This property can be used alongside the license property which indicates license(s) applicable to some piece of content. The usageInfo property can provide information about other licensing options, e.g. acquiring commercial usage rights for an image that is also available under non-commercial creative commons licenses.

attribute.name: value
attribute.description:
The value of a [[QuantitativeValue]] (including [[Observation]]) or property value node.

* For [[QuantitativeValue]] and [[MonetaryAmount]], the recommended type for values is 'Number'.
* For [[PropertyValue]], it can be 'Text', 'Number', 'Boolean', or 'StructuredValue'.
* Use values from 0123456789 (Unicode 'DIGIT ZERO' (U+0030) to 'DIGIT NINE' (U+0039)) rather than superficially similar Unicode symbols.
* Use '.' (Unicode 'FULL STOP' (U+002E)) rather than ',' to indicate a decimal point. Avoid using these symbols as a readability separator.

A case series can be retrospective or prospective and usually involves a smaller number of patients than the more powerful case-control studies or randomized controlled trials. Case series may be consecutive or non-consecutive, depending on whether all cases presenting to the reporting authors over a period of time were included, or only a selection.

attribute.name: CohortStudy
attribute.description: Also known as a panel study. A cohort study is a form of longitudinal study used in medicine and social science. It is one type of study design and should be compared with a cross-sectional study. A cohort is a group of people who share a common characteristic or experience within a defined period (e.g., are born, leave school, lose their job, are exposed to a drug or a vaccine, etc.). The comparison group may be the general population from which the cohort is drawn, or it may be another cohort of persons thought to have had little or no exposure to the substance under investigation, but otherwise similar. Alternatively, subgroups within the cohort may be compared with each other.

attribute.name: DecontextualizedContent
attribute.description:
Content coded 'missing context' in a [[MediaReview]], considered in the context of how it was published or shared.
For a [[VideoObject]] to be 'missing context': Presenting unaltered video in an inaccurate manner that misrepresents the footage. For example, using incorrect dates or locations, altering the transcript or sharing brief clips from a longer video to mislead viewers. (A video rated 'original' can also be missing context.)
For an [[ImageObject]] to be 'missing context': Presenting unaltered images in an inaccurate manner to misrepresent the image and mislead the viewer. For example, a common tactic is using an unaltered image but saying it came from a different time or place. (An image rated 'original' can also be missing context.)
For an [[ImageObject]] with embedded text to be 'missing context': An unaltered image presented in an inaccurate manner to misrepresent the image and mislead the viewer. For example, a common tactic is using an unaltered image but saying it came from a different time or place. (An 'original' image with inaccurate text would generally fall in this category.)
For an [[AudioObject]] to be 'missing context': Unaltered audio presented in an inaccurate manner that misrepresents it. For example, using incorrect dates or locations, or sharing brief clips from a longer recording to mislead viewers. (Audio rated “original” can also be missing context.)

For an [[ImageObject]] to be 'edited or cropped content': Presenting a part of an image from a larger whole to mislead the viewer.
For an [[ImageObject]] with embedded text to be 'edited or cropped content': Presenting a part of an image from a larger whole to mislead the viewer.
For an [[AudioObject]] to be 'edited or cropped content': The audio has been edited or rearranged. This category applies to time edits, including editing multiple audio clips together to alter the story being told or editing out large portions from the recording.

In clinical care, the term is used to designate a branch of medicine using laboratory tests to diagnose and determine the prognostic significance of illness.

attribute.name: PublicHolidays
attribute.description: This stands for any day that is a public holiday; it is a placeholder for all official public holidays in some particular location. While not technically a "day of the week", it can be used with [[OpeningHoursSpecification]]. In the context of an opening hours specification it can be used to indicate opening hours on public holidays, overriding general opening hours for the day of the week on which a public holiday occurs.

attribute.name: SatireOrParodyContent
attribute.description:
Content coded 'satire or parody content' in a [[MediaReview]], considered in the context of how it was published or shared.
For a [[VideoObject]] to be 'satire or parody content': A video that was created as political or humorous commentary and is presented in that context. (Reshares of satire/parody content that do not include relevant context are more likely to fall under the “missing context” rating.)
For an [[ImageObject]] to be 'satire or parody content': An image that was created as political or humorous commentary and is presented in that context. (Reshares of satire/parody content that do not include relevant context are more likely to fall under the “missing context” rating.)
For an [[ImageObject]] with embedded text to be 'satire or parody content': An image that was created as political or humorous commentary and is presented in that context. (Reshares of satire/parody content that do not include relevant context are more likely to fall under the “missing context” rating.)
For an [[AudioObject]] to be 'satire or parody content': Audio that was created as political or humorous commentary and is presented in that context. (Reshares of satire/parody content that do not include relevant context are more likely to fall under the “missing context” rating.)

attribute.name: TransformedContent
attribute.description:
Content coded 'transformed content' in a [[MediaReview]], considered in the context of how it was published or shared.
For a [[VideoObject]] to be 'transformed content': or all of the video has been manipulated to transform the footage itself. This category includes using tools like the Adobe Suite to change the speed of the video, add or remove visual elements or dub audio. Deepfakes are also a subset of transformation.
For an [[ImageObject]] to be 'transformed content': Adding or deleting visual elements to give the image a different meaning with the intention to mislead.
For an [[ImageObject]] with embedded text to be 'transformed content': Adding or deleting visual elements to give the image a different meaning with the intention to mislead.
For an [[AudioObject]] to be 'transformed content': Part or all of the audio has been manipulated to alter the words or sounds, or the audio has been synthetically generated, such as to create a sound-alike voice.
